title: npm releases publish unattended: the npm-publish environment keeps no required reviewers
context: release.yml publishes from the GitHub environment `npm-publish` because npm trusted publishing is bound to that environment name. Since 2026-07-23 the environment also carried a required-reviewer rule (davesheffer). In practice the agent session cutting each release approved it through the API (v1.32.8, v1.33.0), so the rule added a hidden pause and no independent check. On 2026-09-14 that approval call was refused by the host's permission gate and v1.34.0 sat unapproved for two hours; it was never published. David (2026-09-15): make releases unattended.
decision: Remove the required-reviewers protection rule from the `npm-publish` environment and keep the environment itself (same name, no wait timer, no branch policy). A version-tag push is the release authority: main is protected by five required checks, the release workflow re-validates on a clean checkout plus Windows/macOS matrices, and publish proceeds without a human click. rb_cut_release_01 step 9 documents how to detect a re-added rule.
consequences: Anyone able to push a v* tag can publish; tag pushes are limited to repository writers.
A `publish: waiting` job reappearing means a protection rule was re-added; the runbook says how to approve or remove it.
1.34.0 stays unpublished and is documented as superseded before publication.
alternatives_rejected: Keep the reviewer and let the agent approve: restores the previous behaviour but the approval was never an independent check, only a click the same agent performed.
Delete the environment: npm trusted publishing is configured against the environment name; deleting it breaks authentication for every future tag.
Replace the reviewer with a wait timer: delays every release without adding verification.
